comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE — a concern I raised against this row's framing, checked and WITHDRAWN. Recorded so the planner does not spend a step re-opening it.

In #workers (msg-c3a6d207) I warned that this might not be a stale assertion but an OVER-REDACTION defect in DONE task-c78140e9 — the theory being that `docker: not found` carries no secret, so blanketing it would mean that row traded a leak for a blindfold and every operator-facing refusal detail on this path went opaque. That theory is FALSE. I read the implementation; the filer's framing is correct and this row is aimed at the right side.

Why it is false, from `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts` (note: `deployment/`, not `deploy/` as the description says — worth fixing so nobody greps the wrong path):
- `declassifyRefusal` keeps `code` and `layer` ALWAYS and declassifies only the free-text `detail`. `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` is itself a member of `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`, so the vocabulary every reader routes on is untouched. Nothing went opaque.
- The redacted value is raw tool stderr off `lastStderrLine`, which is the untrusted class by construction, not a benign message caught by a clumsy matcher.
- The allowlist is deliberate and its rationale is written at :30-38: a detector CANNOT recognise these secrets — an environment value is opaque and arrives inside a 600-byte stderr tail with no scheme, delimiter or header to match on. So the defence is a finite set of production-minted strings rather than pattern-matching. Membership is EXACT — no trim, no prefix, no case folding — precisely because `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is how a secret rides beside a safe word.

So DoD 1 is correctly aimed: update the consumer to the shipped redaction contract, keep the exact code/layer/dispatch-stage checks, and do not weaken production redaction. Concretely, do NOT "fix" this by adding `docker: not found` — or any stderr-derived string — to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`. That set may only ever contain strings minted by production code with no caller text in them; widening it to satisfy a test would reintroduce exactly the leak c78140e9 closed, and would do it in the one place designed to prevent it.

One process fact for whoever grades this: c78140e9 was gated on the daemon and control-room legs, and this red only appears in the browser lane, which was not in its gate set. The gate set did not reach the consumer; no reviewer skipped a step.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS — add `docker: not found` to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`. The governor names this explicitly as the wrong fix: that set may only ever hold strings MINTED BY PRODUCTION CODE. `docker: not found` is tool stderr, and admitting one stderr-derived string to the allowlist reopens exactly the leak the parent row closed.

REJECTED — export `REDACTED_DETAIL` from deploy-ledger.ts and import it in the spec. This looks like the rail-1 "assert against the production surface" move and it is wrong HERE, for a documented reason: an arm that imports the production marker follows that value ANYWHERE, including to the empty string, and stays green while redaction is gone. Both existing daemon arms declare their own local literal for this exact reason (deploy-journey.test.ts:90, deploy-service.test.ts:63), and the constant is deliberately unexported (deploy-ledger.ts:24). Follow that precedent; do not "improve" it.

REJECTED — rewrite the arm in the value-free boolean shape (`expect(actual === REDACTED).toBe(true)`) that the parent row used for its secrets arms. That shape exists because vitest prints the ACTUAL value on failure, so a `toBe` against a real credential leaks it into the run log at the moment the arm fires. There is no secret here: `docker: not found` is benign stderr from an injected fake. Adopting the value-free shape would trade a readable diff for protection against nothing.

REJECTED — delete or skip the arm. It is the only consumer that noticed the redaction shipped; the browser lane was not in the parent row's gate set, which is why nothing else caught it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-08. This is a genuinely one-line defect with a well-documented contract behind it; the value of this plan is the three traps around that line, not the line.

THE DEFECT, exactly located. tests/e2e/control-room/deploy-fake-docker.spec.ts:179-182 asserts the durable receipt's refusal with `toEqual({ code: mode, layer: "DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE", detail: "docker: not found" })`. EVERY ASSERTING CONSUMER IS NAMED (project rail 20 — grep the shape, not just the symbol). `git grep -rn "docker: not found" -- apps/** packages/** tests/** adapters/** tools/**` returns exactly TWO hits:

  - tests/e2e/control-room/deploy-fake-docker.spec.ts:181 — the stale assertion.
There is no third consumer, so this row is genuinely one file.

THE CALL SITE IS SINGULAR. The assertion sits inside `for (const mode of ["SUCCESS", "DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE"] as const)` at :149, in the non-SUCCESS branch of a ternary — so only DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE reaches it and no sibling mode asserts a different detail. The file holds four tests total: the two parameterized ones, a paired-human publish arm at :211, and a teardown-on-throw arm at :229 (which is the teardown evidence DoD 2 asks for).

THE REDACTION CONTRACT, read rather than assumed (apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts — note `deployment/`, NOT `deploy/` as the row description says):
- `declassifyRefusal` (:50-54) keeps `code` and `layer` ALWAYS and declassifies only the free-text `detail`.
- `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` (:39-46) is a finite allowlist of strings minted by production code with no caller text in them. `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` is itself a member, so the vocabulary readers route on is untouched. The redacted value here is raw tool stderr off `lastStderrLine` — untrusted by construction.
- Membership is EXACT: no trim, no prefix, no case folding, because `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is precisely how a secret rides beside a safe word (:36-38).

THE GOVERNOR ALREADY CLOSED THE ALTERNATIVE READING (comment-f6f65323). They raised and then WITHDREW the theory that this is over-redaction in the DONE row: it is not, the filer's framing is correct, and the fix belongs on the consumer. Do not spend a step reopening it.

The negative in step 2 (the raw stderr appears NOWHERE in the receipt) is what keeps it a REDACTION arm rather than a string comparison, and it is the half that survives a future field carrying the stderr through another path.

2. DO NOT WIDEN INTO THE PARENT ROW'S FILES. apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts and deploy-ports.ts are read-only for this row. They are named in keyFiles so the worker can READ the contract, and they are deliberately absent from every step's affectedFiles.

3. THE BROWSER LANE IS A SHARED, LEASED RESOURCE. DoD 2 requires the FULL spec file, not the `-g` filtered run the filing used. Acquire `browser-e2e-gate` before the run and release it after; a concurrent lane is how these runs become unattributable.

4. THE FILE'S OTHER THREE TESTS ARE NOT THIS ROW'S. If the paired-human publish arm (:211) or the teardown arm (:229) is red, attribute it by path against the merge-base baseline (global rail 3) and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it.

5. FOREIGN DIRT IS PRESENT and is not a stop condition: seven paths belong to other sessions, including tests/e2e/control-room/deploy-migrations.spec.ts, a SIBLING of the file this row edits. Note it, never revert or commit it.
